questions.question: 1. Magnifying power (m) of simple microscope is (where D is the least distance of distinct vision for humans, and F if the focal length of the convex lens) :

explanations.a: Incorrect. D/F is the magnifying power when the final image is formed at infinity.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The magnifying power is greater than 1 and is not given by F/D.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This expression is not the formula for the magnifying power of a simple microscope.
explanations.d: Correct. When the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision (D), the magnifying power of a simple microscope is (D/F) + 1.

questions.question: 2. The magnifying power (m) of compound microscope with an objective and eyepiece is (where D is the least distance of distinct vision, L is the length of the microscope tube, f<sub>o</sub> is the focal length of the objective lens, and f<sub>e</sub> is the focal length of the eyepiece) :

explanations.a: Correct. The magnifying power of a compound microscope is approximately m = (L/f<sub>o</sub>) × (D/f<sub>e</sub>) = DL/(f<sub>o</sub>f<sub>e</sub>).
explanations.b: Incorrect. The positions of L and fe are interchanged, giving an incorrect expression.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This formula does not represent the magnifying power of a compound microscope.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is the reciprocal of the correct formula.

questions.question: 3. In a phase contrast microscope, phase shift DOES NOT occur in the samples due to :

answers.a: difference in the thickness of region

explanations.a: Incorrect. Differences in sample thickness can cause phase shifts in transmitted light.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Variations in refractive index of cellular structures or organelles produce phase shifts.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The orientation of crystalline materials can affect the phase of transmitted light.
explanations.d: Correct. A homogeneous sample with uniform composition and refractive index does not produce phase differences and therefore does not cause phase shift.

questions.question: 4. Due to dark background, a very high contrast is obtained in which microscope :

explanations.a: Incorrect. A compound microscope uses transmitted light and does not typically produce a dark background.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A phase contrast microscope enhances contrast through phase differences but does not create a dark background.
explanations.c: Correct. In a fluorescence microscope, the background appears dark while the fluorescent specimen emits bright light, resulting in very high contrast.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A stereo microscope provides a three-dimensional view but does not produce a dark background.

questions.question: 5. A 3-dimensional appearance of fractured samples can be observed in which of the following microscope ?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A compound microscope provides a two-dimensional image of the specimen.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A phase contrast microscope enhances contrast in transparent specimens but does not provide a true 3D appearance.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A fluorescence microscope is used to visualize fluorescently labeled structures, not for 3D observation of fractured surfaces.
explanations.d: Correct. A stereo microscope provides a three-dimensional view of the specimen, making it suitable for observing fractured surfaces and surface features.

questions.question: 6. Which microscope permits dye-staining for identification of living/dead cells and various organelles :

explanations.a: Incorrect. A compound microscope can use stains, but it is not specifically designed for identifying living/dead cells through fluorescent dyes.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A phase contrast microscope is mainly used for observing unstained living cells.
explanations.c: Correct. A fluorescence microscope uses fluorescent dyes to identify living and dead cells and to visualize specific organelles with high contrast.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A stereo microscope is used for observing surface features and does not typically use fluorescent dye staining.
